author: @foxnews
title_or_hook: Somebody hit us: the Copa/UPS taxiway collision at Miami (VERIFIED in full; the feed lead telling of a three-telling event)
summary: VERIFIED this run across the FAA account as reported by CNN and Simple Flying: at about 9:15 PM on Sat Nov 14, the left wingtip of Copa Airlines flight 427 (Boeing 737-800, just landed from Panama City, 166 passengers plus 6 crew) struck the nose of UPS flight 358 (Boeing 767 freighter, taxiing for departure to Bogota) at a taxiway intersection. Controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way; the UPS pilot own transmission concedes they went too far. Two passengers were evaluated/treated at the scene for minor injuries; neither was hospitalized. The FAA is investigating. The collision came the day after the Nov 13 nationwide ground stop - investigators have drawn no link between the two. Frame: two planes nose-to-nose at night at Miami airport under emergency lights, with released ATC audio as the on-screen headline; the ATC audio itself is unrecoverable in this read.
